AD1.name: Ad platform sources into CJA, with your client's ad admins
AD1.scope: Authorize the Experience Platform advertising sources for the agreed ad accounts (Google Ads, Meta, Pinterest, Snapchat or TikTok) once your client's ad admins approve access in each network, then add the paid media datasets the sources create to the CJA connection and data view as summary data.

references.title: Join Paid Media Data With Web Data In Customer Journey Analytics

AD2.name: Ad spend joined to web conversions: ROAS and cost per web order
AD2.src: Experience League: CJA, paid media use case
AD2.scope: Build derived fields that read the network and campaign IDs from landing page URLs, set up summary data groups, and build Workspace reports for web ROAS, cost per web order and the gap between what the networks report and what the site records.

AD3.name: Ad platform destinations: account access, hashed identities and match-rate checks
AD3.src: Experience League: Experience Platform, advertising destinations
AD3.scope: For each agreed ad destination, connect with your client's permitted ad account, map its supported identities, apply its normalization and hashing rules, activate a first audience, and review the platform's reported match rates where available.

BI1.name: BI extension setup and number check
BI1.scope: Set up Query Service and data view permissions with your client's admin, connect each agreed BI tool, and check that its numbers match Analysis Workspace.

BI2.name: Executive dashboards in your client's BI tool
BI2.scope: Build the agreed dashboards on CJA data views within the BI extension's limits (aggregate data, 50,000 rows a query, a 30-day default range).

SD1.name: Search Console and GA4 connections, and prompts picked from search queries
SD1.src: Experience League: Brand Visibility, brands management
SD1.scope: Connect Search Console, and GA4 where your client does not have CJA, to each agreed brand's onboarded domain with someone on your client's side who has the right Google permissions, then review the suggested queries and pick the prompts to track by brand and market.

references.title: Experience League: Prompt Management (Prompt Strategy, Google Search Console suggestions)
Experience League: Customer Configuration, Google Search Console (legacy reference page)

CS1.name: Document authoring setup with your client's Microsoft 365 or Google admin, and author training
CS1.src: aem.live: SharePoint as a content source
CS1.scope: Plan the site and root folder with your client's IT, run Adobe's app registration and site grant with their Microsoft 365 admin (or share the Google Drive folder), set the site configuration, check preview and publish in Sidekick, and train the authors.

references.title: Configure Your Content Source for Edge Delivery Services

CS2.name: Sites Optimizer write-back to SharePoint or Google Drive
CS2.scope: Connect Sites Optimizer to the documents (an app registration with a client secret on your client's SharePoint, or a Google Drive folder share), check the connection, deploy one eligible pilot content fix using that opportunity's documented write-back route, and plan the secret's rotation.

CM1.name: Brand Concierge script and surface rules through your client's tag manager
CM1.scope: Add the Brand Concierge script through your client's tag manager or page templates, choose the component or full-page install, write the surface rules and test an included and an excluded page.

CM2.name: Website Links knowledge source and refresh
CM2.src: Experience League: Brand Concierge, knowledge sources
CM2.scope: Choose the sitemap, URLs or CSV for the site, set the refresh schedule, and fix the failed URLs the Fix Issues report lists.

CR1.name: Customer Attributes from the CRM into Target
CR1.scope: Export the agreed attributes from the CRM, line up the customer ID with how the site identifies visitors, create the Customer Attributes source, subscribe it to Target and set up the file feed within Adobe's limits.

DW1.name: Warehouse tables into Experience Platform
DW1.scope: Connect the warehouse source with your client's data team (allowed IP addresses, the agreed tables), map them to schemas, set incremental loading and the schedule, and check the first load.
DW1.tier: Real-Time CDP Ultimate or the Advanced Enterprise connectors

DW2.name: Data Mirror for orchestrated campaigns
DW2.src: Experience League: Journey Optimizer, orchestrated campaign data
DW2.scope: Design the relational schemas, turn on change tracking in your client's tables with their data team, set up the source and plan how deletes are handled at the source.
DW2.tier: Journey Optimizer Campaigns or Campaigns & Journeys, with Campaign Orchestration

AFX01.name: Adaptive forms on AEM Sites pages
AFX01.src: Experience League: Add an Adaptive Form to an AEM Sites page or Experience Fragment
AFX01.scope: Add the Adaptive Forms client libraries to the site's page components through the deployment pipeline, allow the Adaptive Forms Container in the page templates, and build or embed the first forms on pages and Experience Fragments.
AFX01.evidence: To enable complete functionality of the Adaptive Forms Container component, add the Customheaderlibs and Customfooterlibs client libraries to your AEM Sites page using the deployment pipeline.

AFX02.name: Forms Portal with drafts and submissions
AFX02.src: Experience League: Introduction to Forms Portal
AFX02.scope: Build the forms portal on site pages with the Search & Lister, Drafts & Submissions and Link components, connect your client's Azure Storage through the Unified Storage Connector, and confirm site sign-in, since only signed-in people can resume drafts and see their submissions.
AFX02.evidence: Forms Portal provides an efficient way to display and list Adaptive Forms on an AEM Sites page.

AFX03.name: One theme for site and forms
AFX03.src: Experience League: Embed an Adaptive Forms theme in an AEM Sites theme
AFX03.scope: Embed the Adaptive Forms theme in the AEM Sites theme so one build and one front-end pipeline deployment styles both the pages and the forms on them.
AFX03.evidence: a single theme drives both your site pages and any Adaptive Forms embedded on those pages, with one build and one deployment

AFX04.name: Adaptive Forms Block on Edge Delivery
AFX04.src: Experience League: Getting Started with Edge Delivery Services for AEM Forms using Universal Editor
AFX04.scope: Add the Adaptive Forms Block to the Edge Delivery repository (or start from the AEM Forms boilerplate), connect AEM Code Sync and the AEM author, create forms from the Edge Delivery template in the Universal Editor, and publish them.
AFX04.evidence: This boilerplate offers a ready-to-use template that seamlessly integrates the Adaptive Forms Block, enabling you to quickly build and deploy forms within your AEM Site.

AFX05.name: Edge Delivery form submissions to AEM Publish
AFX05.src: Experience League: Configure Submit Actions for AEM Forms
AFX05.scope: Send Edge Delivery form submissions to AEM Publish so workflows, the Form Data Model and the other submit actions can process them: set the publish URL in the form block, the Referrer Filter and the Dispatcher CORS rules for each site domain, and test.
AFX05.evidence: Submit form data directly to your AEM as a Cloud Service Publish instance for complex processing.

AFX06.name: Document-based forms with spreadsheet submissions
AFX06.src: Experience League: Forms Submission Service for Edge Delivery Services
AFX06.scope: Define simple forms in Google Sheets or Excel, set up the Forms Submission Service so entries land in your client's spreadsheet, and publish each form.
AFX06.evidence: The Forms Submission Service is Adobe's hosted solution that automatically stores form submission data directly in your preferred spreadsheets

AFX07.name: Experience Platform setup for form data
AFX07.src: Experience League: AEM Forms Integration with Adobe Real-Time CDP
AFX07.scope: Create or extend the XDM schema for form data in your client's Experience Platform, enable it for Profile with an identity field, and create the dataset, the streaming connection and the API credentials the connector uses.
AFX07.evidence: Before setting up the AEP Connector in AEM Forms, ensure you have completed the following in Adobe Experience Platform

AFX08.name: Forms on XDM schemas that update profiles
AFX08.src: Experience League: AEM Forms Integration with Adobe Real-Time CDP
AFX08.scope: Create the Experience Platform cloud configuration in AEM, build each form on a profile-enabled XDM schema, set the Submit to Adobe Experience Platform action with the streaming URL and dataflow ID, and check that submissions reach the dataset and the profile.
AFX08.evidence: This integration allows you to create forms using XDM schemas available in Adobe Experience Platform and submit data back to Real-Time CDP for personalization and profile hydration purposes.

AFX09.name: Marketo Engage connection for adaptive forms
AFX09.src: Experience League: Integrate Marketo Engage with AEM Forms
AFX09.scope: Create the Marketo Engage cloud configuration in AEM with a LaunchPoint custom service's Client ID and Client Secret and the REST Identity URL, and confirm the connection.
AFX09.evidence: The Cloud configuration connects your Experience Manager instance to the Adobe Marketo Engage instance.

AFX10.name: Forms mapped and submitted to Marketo
AFX10.src: Experience League: Configure the submit action to Marketo Engage for existing forms
AFX10.scope: Build new forms on the Marketo Engage data model in the form wizard, or bind existing forms to it, set the Submit to Marketo Engage action, and test that submissions reach the People database.
AFX10.evidence: Adaptive Forms editor provides the Submit to Marketo Engage submit action to send Adaptive Forms data to Adobe Marketo Engage for processing.

AFX11.name: Form submissions into Workfront Fusion
AFX11.src: Experience League: Submit an Adaptive Form to Adobe Workfront Fusion
AFX11.scope: Build the Fusion scenario that starts with the AEM Forms module and a webhook, connect it with the AEM service credentials, add the technical account to the forms-users group, and set the form's submit action to invoke the scenario.
AFX11.evidence: AEM Forms as a Cloud Service provides an OOTB connector to connect and submit an Adaptive Form to Adobe Workfront Fusion.

AFX12.name: Workfront work created from form data
AFX12.src: Experience League: Submit an Adaptive Form to Adobe Workfront Fusion
AFX12.scope: Extend the scenario so each submission starts the right work in Workfront, such as a project, assigned tasks, notifications or a status update, and test it with your client's request types.
AFX12.evidence: This can include initiating projects, assigning tasks to specific team members, sending notifications, and updating project statuses

AFX13.name: Coworker form drafts and edits
AFX13.scope: Pilot Coworker creating and updating adaptive forms from briefs, screenshots or PDFs: prepare the guidelines document and the templates and themes on the author instance that it picks from, write the prompts your client's team will reuse, and set the review step before a form is published.
AFX13.evidence: You describe the Adaptive Form or change you need, and the AI builds or updates it directly in your Experience Manager environment, then returns a link so you can review or continue customizing it.

AFX14.name: Connectors and services ready for Coworker
AFX14.scope: Configure the submit connectors, Form Data Model services and custom functions in AEM first, since Coworker only uses ones that already exist, then test the rule and submission prompts with your client's team.
AFX14.evidence: The connector must already be configured in Experience Manager before the Form submission configuration skill can select and set it.

AFX15.name: PDF and XDP imports with Coworker
AFX15.scope: Store your client's existing PDF and XDP forms in the AEM DAM, import them into adaptive forms with Coworker, then review each form's fields, rules and layout in the editor.
AFX15.evidence: Convert a PDF or XDP stored in AEM DAM into an Adaptive Form.

XB12.name: Workfront to AEM Assets integration
XB12.src: Experience League: Configure the Experience Manager Assets as a Cloud Service integration (Workfront)
XB12.scope: Connect Workfront to the Experience Manager Assets repository, map Workfront fields to asset metadata, and, in Workfront's classic Documents area, set up linked folder trees and the workflows on project templates that create folders and publish assets (they are not available in the new Documents area).
XB12.evidence: Push assets and metadata from Adobe Workfront to Experience Manager Assets

AXA01.name: Move from the old Workfront connector
AXA01.src: Experience League: Migrate from the legacy or enhanced connector to the native AEM Assets integration (Workfront)
AXA01.scope: Where your client is still on the legacy or enhanced connector: move existing linked folders and documents to the native integration, validate the critical use cases, then uninstall the old connector, which cannot run alongside the native one.
AXA01.evidence: It will be important to validate all critical use cases intended to be used through the native integration prior to uninstalling the legacy or enhanced connector.

AXA02.name: Fusion automations with AEM Assets
AXA02.src: Experience League: Adobe Experience Manager Assets modules (Workfront Fusion)
AXA02.scope: Where the native integration stops short, set up the server-to-server credentials with write access and build Workfront Fusion scenarios with the AEM Assets connector, such as metadata updates, asset imports from a URL, or scenarios that start when an asset changes in AEM.
AXA02.evidence: With the Adobe Experience Manager Assets connector for Adobe Workfront Fusion, you can create, upload, and update assets, and copy or move folders and assets.
AXA02.ext: Workfront Fusion (part of Workfront Ultimate and of Workflow plus Automation and Integration packages; Prime and Select need it bought separately)

AXA03.name: Planning campaigns linked to AEM assets
AXA03.scope: Where your client has Workfront Planning, connect record types such as campaigns to AEM Assets, choose the lookup fields to show, agree how teams link images, folders and Content Fragments to records.
AXA03.evidence: After you create a connection between a record type and Adobe Experience Manager objects, you can connect individual records to Experience Manager objects.

AXA04.name: AEM page data collection for CJA
AXA04.src: Experience League: Integrate AEM Sites and Experience Platform Web SDK
AXA04.scope: Connect the Tags property to AEM through its IMS and cloud configurations, build data elements from the AEM Core Components data layer (page name, site section, host), send page views with Web SDK, check that they reach the dataset, then add the dataset to the CJA connection and data view.
AXA04.evidence: Rule: Send data to Platform Edge Network whenever a WKND webpage is visited using the Adobe Client Data Layer triggered cmp:show event.

references.title: Customer Journey Analytics quick start guide

AXA05.name: CTA click tracking from the AEM data layer
AXA05.src: Experience League: CTA collection and Platform dataset verification
AXA05.scope: Add a Tags rule on the data layer's click event for the site's buttons and teaser CTAs, send the CTA ID and name with Web SDK, and check the clicks in the dataset before they are added to the CJA data view.
AXA05.evidence: The Dataset created in the previous tutorial is reused to verify that the pageview and CTA click data is ingested into the Experience Platform Dataset.

references.title: Customer Journey Analytics quick start guide

AXA06.name: Custom components in the data layer
AXA06.src: Experience League: Extending the Adobe Client Data Layer (Core Components)
AXA06.scope: Extend custom component data-layer models with the required author fields, then update Tags/Web SDK mappings and the CJA data view so agreed view and click events include those fields.
AXA06.evidence: You can extend the Core Components with custom dialog options that allow content authors to enter additional information related to the Data Layer.

references.title: Integrate AEM Sites and Experience Platform Web SDK
Customer Journey Analytics quick start guide

AXA07.name: AEM visitors into profiles
AXA07.src: Experience League: Behavioral Targeting (AEM as a Cloud Service tutorial)
AXA07.scope: Send the AEM page views to a profile-enabled dataset under the agreed identities, check that visits build profiles under the right merge policy, and confirm the first behavior-based audience. The Tags property on AEM pages comes with Real-Time CDP's data ingestion setup, or with AEM page data collection for CJA when CJA is on the canvas.
AXA07.evidence: To create audiences based on behavioral data, it is necessary to collect and store data when users visit or interact with your website.

AXA08.name: Known visitors from the AEM login
AXA08.src: Experience League: Known-user personalization (AEM as a Cloud Service tutorial)
AXA08.scope: Where the site has a login, make the AEM user ID available to Tags and send it in Web SDK's identity map under your client's own namespace, so site visits join CRM or order data in one profile.
AXA08.evidence: Enhance the WKND site Login functionality to store the user id in the browser's session storage.

AXB02.name: Experience Fragments as Target offers
AXB02.src: Experience League: Exporting Experience Fragments to Adobe Target
AXB02.scope: Set up the Developer Console project and the IMS, Target and legacy Target configurations in AEM, configure the Link Externalizer, set export format, workspace and domain on the fragment folders, and set up the publish, export and update routine for lean Web variations.
AXB02.evidence: They can then be used as offers in Target activities, to test and personalize experiences at scale.

references.title: How Do I Use Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) Experience Fragments?

AXB03.name: Content Fragment offers for headless apps
AXB03.src: Experience League: Integrate AEM Headless and Target
AXB03.scope: For headless apps, apply the Target configuration to the Content Fragment folders, give the integration the Editor role in the Admin Console, export fragments as JSON offers for Form-based activities, and check the app renders them through Web SDK.
AXB03.evidence: You can export Content Fragments, created in Adobe Experience Manager as a Cloud Service (AEM), to Adobe Target (Target).

references.title: Exporting Content Fragments to Adobe Target
How Do I Use Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) Content Fragments?

AXB05.name: Link AEM Assets to Marketo Engage
AXB05.src: Experience League: Work with Experience Manager assets (Marketo Engage)
AXB05.scope: Confirm the Marketo subscription is on Adobe IMS (the Email Designer needs it) and Dynamic Media with OpenAPI is on, generate the service credential certificate, link the Delivery tier repository in Marketo Admin, add email authors to the Assets product profiles, and track the certificate expiry.
AXB05.evidence: Before you can use this capability, you must first link AEM Cloud Services with Adobe Marketo Engage.

AXB06.name: Email templates on AEM Assets images
AXB06.src: Experience League: Work with Experience Manager assets (Marketo Engage)
AXB06.scope: Set AEM Assets as the image source on your client's email templates and visual fragments, swap images stored in Marketo for DAM-linked ones, and agree who may change or delete images used in live emails, since a deleted image breaks them.
AXB06.evidence: you can designate AEM Assets as the source for assets when you create or view details for an email, email template, or visual fragment.

AXC01.name: Optimize at Edge on the AEM managed CDN
AXC01.src: Experience League: Optimize at Edge, AEM Cloud Service Managed CDN (Fastly)
AXC01.scope: Where the AEM managed CDN is the site's outer CDN, enable Brand Visibility's routing for AI agents in the Brand Visibility UI, then test that agent requests return the x-edgeoptimize-request-id header while visitors and search bots still get AEM's pages. If the Edge Delivery build already covers routing for this domain, reserve this service for another domain with an AEM-managed outer CDN.
AXC01.evidence: This configuration routes agentic traffic (requests from AI bots and LLM user agents) to the Edge Optimize backend service (live.edgeoptimize.net).

AXC03.name: AEM publish readiness for Brand Visibility
AXC03.src: Experience League: Brand Visibility, Optimize at Edge
AXC03.scope: Allow the AdobeEdgeOptimize/1.0 user agent in the AEM site's robots.txt and traffic filter rules, and make sure pages leave Dispatcher and the CDN with a Last-Modified header, so content fixes are not skipped.
AXC03.evidence: If the Last-Modified header is absent, the optimization is skipped, since there is no reliable signal to detect that the page has been updated.

AXC05.name: Connect Sites Optimizer to AEM author
AXC05.src: Experience League: Sites Optimizer release notes
AXC05.scope: Choose the Sites Optimizer delivery type that serves the public site. Use Edge Delivery Services for Edge-delivered pages, AEM Cloud Service for cloud Publish delivery, or AEM Managed Services for managed Publish delivery. Connect the AEM author environment as the content provider and verify permissions with an eligible content change in author. Reuse the site activation and initial deployment from Sites Optimizer setup when those are already in scope.
AXC05.evidence: Adobe documents delivery type and the content provider separately and recognizes AEM-authored Edge Delivery Services configurations.

AXC06.name: Code fixes through the Cloud Manager repository
AXC06.src: Experience League: Sites Optimizer release notes
AXC06.scope: For Cloud Manager bring-your-own Git, configure pull-request delivery; for Cloud Manager standard repositories, configure branch delivery. Agree developer review, testing and release.
AXC06.evidence: Code-patch autofix for opportunities like Core Web Vitals, Security, and Form Accessibility can now raise pull requests on Cloud Manager bring-your-own-git repositories hosted on GitHub

AXC07.name: Preflight in AEM authoring
AXC07.src: Experience League: Sites Optimizer Preflight setup
AXC07.scope: Turn on Preflight where AEM authors work (the Page Editor toolbar on a supported AEM version, or the Universal Editor extension a system administrator enables), assign the Auto-Suggest or Auto-Optimize profiles, and train authors to run SEO and accessibility audits before they publish.
AXC07.evidence: If your author environment is running AEM 2026.7.0 (release 27083) or later, Preflight is built into the AEM Sites Page Editor and no bookmarklet is required.

AXC08.name: Multi-site rules for Sites Optimizer fixes
AXC08.src: Experience League: Sites Optimizer release notes
AXC08.scope: For supported opportunity types, document whether to update the source or a local page, including any intended inheritance break; obtain approval and test the affected variants.
AXC08.evidence: When generating Alt Text fixes for sites that use AEM Multi-Site Manager or Language Copy, Sites Optimizer now checks whether fixes can be safely applied to each language variant before suggesting them.

AXD01.name: AEM Sites as the Edge Delivery content source
AXD01.src: Experience League: Create an AEM site (Edge Delivery Services with the Universal Editor tutorial)
AXD01.scope: Create the site on AEM Author from the Edge Delivery Services with AEM authoring template, link the Edge Delivery code to it as the content source, give the publishing technical account its rights, set the path mapping, and add a separate production site where stage and production are split.
AXD01.evidence: To create an AEM site delivered via Edge Delivery Services and authored using Universal Editor, use the Edge Delivery Services with AEM authoring site template to create a new site on AEM Author.

references.title: Authoring with AEM Sites for Edge Delivery Services
How content is published from AEM Sites authoring to Edge Delivery Services

AXD02.name: Blocks set up for the Universal Editor
AXD02.src: Experience League: Create a new block (Edge Delivery Services with the Universal Editor tutorial)
AXD02.scope: Give each block in the library its Universal Editor definition, model and filter so authors can add and edit it in AEM, and check that pages publish to Edge Delivery as expected. The block code and styles stay in the Edge Delivery build.
AXD02.evidence: Registers the block as an editable component in the Universal Editor, linking it to a block model and optionally a filter.

AXD03.name: Localized Edge Delivery sites with MSM
AXD03.src: aem.live: Multi site management with AEM authoring as your content source
AXD03.scope: Turn on repoless for the project, give each localized MSM site its own AEM configuration and Edge Delivery site on the shared code base, and check that Live Copy rollouts publish to the right site.
AXD03.evidence: Your localized sites can then each be delivered by Edge Delivery Services, leveraging a central code base.

AXD04.name: AEM publish and Edge Delivery on one domain
AXD04.src: Experience League: Configuring Traffic at the CDN
AXD04.scope: For a phased move, agree which paths move in each phase, route them to Edge Delivery with origin selector rules in the CDN configuration deployed through the config pipeline, set up push invalidation, and keep the other pages on AEM publish until they move.
AXD04.evidence: Some content is delivered by a domain managed by AEM Publish, while other content from the same domain is delivered by Edge Delivery Services.

AXD07.name: Publishing DAM assets to Edge Delivery
AXD07.src: aem.live: Publishing pages with AEM Assets
AXD07.scope: For sites authored in AEM, grant the publishing technical account access to private asset folders, include the required DAM paths in the site mapping, and assign the site's cloud configuration to folders used for independent asset publishing. Configure compliant Edge Delivery renditions, assign the processing profile to the agreed folders, and reprocess existing assets.
AXD07.evidence: the assets, especially images and videos, must adhere to the limits of Edge Delivery

AXD05.name: AEM Assets picker for site authors
AXD05.src: Experience League: Integrate AEM Assets while authoring content for Edge Delivery Services
AXD05.scope: Set up the asset picker authors will use, the AEM Assets Sidekick plugin in Word or Google Docs or the custom asset picker in the Universal Editor, with the agreed repositories, filters and copy or reference mode.
AXD05.evidence: Configure the AEM Assets Sidekick plugin to use assets while authoring content in Microsoft Word or Google Docs.

AXD06.name: Responsive Dynamic Media images on Edge Delivery
AXD06.src: Experience League: Imported images render as static instead of responsive assets in AEM Edge Delivery Services
AXD06.scope: Where your client has Dynamic Media with OpenAPI, place approved assets by reference and update the block code so delivery URLs render as responsive images with width, crop, format and quality settings, plus video and PDF links.
AXD06.evidence: Update your importer or EDS block logic to generate responsive image markup by using the AEM Assets delivery URL.

references.title: Integrate AEM Assets while authoring content for Edge Delivery Services

AXD08.name: Coworker page drafts from reference pages
AXD08.scope: Choose and tidy an approved reference page for each page type, write a brief template with goals, audience and keywords, pilot Coworker drafting pages that open in the Page Editor or Universal Editor.
AXD08.evidence: It uses a natural language prompt together with a marketing brief to provide guidance, and an AEM reference page as a template for the layout.

AXD09.name: Coworker for AEM developers and operations
AXD09.src: Experience League: Development Agentic Capabilities Overview
AXD09.scope: Agree which pipeline and environment actions may run through Coworker and which need a second review, and add Troubleshoot with AI and Dispatcher Insights to the release and support runbook.
AXD09.evidence: To use the AEM Cloud Manager Pipeline Troubleshooting skill, you must have either the Developer or the Program Manager role in Cloud Manager.

AXD10.name: Visual Content Fragments from Figma
AXD10.src: Experience League: Figma to Visual Content Fragments Skill
AXD10.scope: Store the Figma access token in AEM, import approved Figma designs with Coworker, then review the Content Fragment models, fragments and templates it creates, reusing existing models where they fit.

AXD16.name: Asset rights, Content Hub access rules and permission fixes

XQ03.name: Program inventory and move plan from Marketo Engage
XQ03.scope: List your client's Marketo Engage programs, use Coworker's migration stories to decide which stay in Marketo Engage and which are rebuilt as Marketo Optimizer programs and journeys, check the images copied from Design Studio and upload any that changed, and agree the order of the move.
XQ03.evidence: Generate migration stories from Marketo Engage programs for Marketo Optimizer adaptation.

XQ04.name: Coworker access and skills rollout in Marketo Optimizer
XQ04.src: Experience League: Coworker chat interface (Marketo Optimizer)
XQ04.scope: Give your client's users the permissions Coworker needs, decide which roles may create and publish through chat and which may only read, write a starter prompt library for your client's common tasks and pilot it with the marketing team.
XQ04.evidence: The system checks every skill or action in chat against the same permissions that the feature needs outside chat

XQ05.name: Campaign brief template and programs built by Coworker
XQ05.src: Experience League: Create a program from a brief (Marketo Optimizer)
XQ05.scope: Write the campaign brief template your client's team fills in, with the program type, audience criteria, journey design and tokens Coworker looks for, build the first programs from real briefs, and run Coworker's check on each before launch.
XQ05.evidence: the Program Creation skill builds that entire structure end-to-end from your brief

XQ06.name: Custom Coworker skills for your client's processes
XQ06.scope: Create custom skills for the tasks your client's team repeats, such as a weekly journey readout or a pre-launch check, test and refine each with the people who will use it, and document what it reads and what it changes.
XQ06.evidence: These skills answer product questions and let you build new custom skills.

XQ09.name: Personas, intent model and AI decisioning data gaps
XQ09.scope: Prepare the data Marketo Optimizer's AI decisioning reads: define up to 10 personas from your client's person attributes in the persona mapping panel, set and activate the intent model's activity weights with Coworker's Intent configuration skill and check the results with Analyze intent, then use AI-decisioning health to find coverage gaps across demographic, firmographic, technographic, psychographic, persona and intent data and agree an enrichment plan for them.
XQ09.evidence: Closing those gaps improves how AI decisioning scores and routes each person.

XQ10.name: Webinar programs with Coworker in Marketo Optimizer
XQ10.src: Experience League: Create and Promote Webinars (Marketo Optimizer)
XQ10.scope: Set up your client's first interactive webinar with Coworker: create the webinar in its program at the licensed capacity, design the registration page and room in the Adobe Connect design surface, build the promotion and post-webinar journeys Coworker drafts, finish what it lists as left to configure (the journey audience, the invitation email, the registration form event filter and the member status steps), test and publish, and leave a reusable webinar program for later events.
XQ10.evidence: The chat interface lists what is left to configure in the journey canvas.

XQ07.name: Ad platform destinations and permissions
XQ07.scope: Add the destination permissions to your client's roles, configure the LinkedIn, Google Customer Match and Facebook destinations your client uses with a sign-in to each ad account, map the people attributes each one needs, and review the data governance and marketing action settings.
XQ07.evidence: Destinations are pre-built integrations that let you send static people lists from Marketo Optimizer to external advertising or social platforms

XQ08.name: Audience activation from lists and journeys
XQ08.src: Experience League: Take an action nodes (Marketo Optimizer)
XQ08.scope: Build the static lists your client's paid media needs, activate each to its destinations, add Activate to destination actions to the journeys that should feed or clear an ad audience, and check with the media team that members arrive and leave as expected.
XQ08.evidence: Use this action to add people to a static list and activate that list to a destination directly from your journey.

XP01.name: Marketing Highlights setup
XP01.src: Experience League: Marketo Qualifier, Set up Marketing Highlights
XP01.scope: Create the API credentials in the Adobe Developer Console, set up the webhook in your client's Marketo Engage with Adobe's payload template matched to the instance's field names, add it to the trigger Smart Campaigns for the activities your client's representatives should see, and check that activity arrives under Marketing Highlights.
XP01.evidence: Marketing Highlights shows each prospect's live Marketo activity, such as email opens and clicks, web visits, and form fills. This article explains how to connect your Marketo instance so that activity flows in.

XP02.name: Sales outreach in Marketo scoring and timelines
XP02.scope: With activity sync on, bring Marketo Qualifier's email sent, opened, clicked and replied activities into your client's Marketo Engage lead scoring and engagement programs, and agree with your client's marketing team how its programs treat prospects in active outreach.
XP02.evidence: Representatives can see the activities in the CRM, while marketing teams can use the Marketo activities in lead scoring and engagement timelines.

XP03.name: Automatic enrollment from live Marketo activity
XP03.src: Experience League: Marketo Qualifier, Outbound Workflows
XP03.scope: Set the targeting criteria on your client's Outbound Workflows so prospects whose live Marketo activity matches are enrolled for the representative who owns them, check owner matching against the CRM, and test the warning for prospects another representative is already contacting.
XP03.evidence: An Outbound Workflow can evaluate live Marketing Highlights activity against its targeting criteria.

XP04.name: Activity sync and CRM Sync Rules
XP04.src: Experience League: Marketo Qualifier, Admin settings
XP04.scope: Arrange write access with your client's CRM administrator, turn on activity sync, and set the CRM Sync Rules: which lead, contact, account or opportunity fields change when a prospect is added, replies, books a meeting, opts out, bounces or finishes with no reply, with tokens for the representative, the workflow and the meeting time. Test each rule against your client's CRM validation rules.
XP04.evidence: Marketo Qualifier can write lead status updates back to Salesforce and Microsoft Dynamics automatically as a prospect moves through an Outbound Workflow, so representatives no longer update the CRM by hand.

XP05.name: CRM plugin and Salesforce actions
XP05.src: Experience League: Marketo Qualifier, CRM Connections (CRM plugin setup)
XP05.scope: Install the Marketo Qualifier plugin in your client's Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics 365, add its components to the Lead, Contact and Account record pages, and in Salesforce add the Add to Outbound Workflow and Add to Marketo Campaign buttons to list views and page layouts, then test each with a representative's login.
XP05.evidence: Install the Adobe Marketo Qualifier CRM plugin so that representatives can use Marketo Sales Insights and AI-generated insights on Lead, Contact, and Account record pages without leaving Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics 365.

XP06.name: Representatives and routing for concierge handoffs
XP06.src: Experience League: Brand Concierge, Set up representatives in Adobe Marketo Qualifier
XP06.scope: Add your client's representatives, help each connect a calendar, write the confirmation email and set calendar and live chat availability, check everyone under Manage members, and choose round robin or a direct agent for meetings and for chats.
XP06.evidence: Before a concierge can offer a meeting or a live chat, at least one representative has to be set up in Adobe Marketo Qualifier.

XP07.name: Live chat and meeting booking in the concierge
XP07.src: Experience League: Brand Concierge, Activate live chat and meeting booking
XP07.scope: Connect the Meeting Booking and Live Chat integrations in Composer, set the Handoff to sales skill's conditions and instructions for your client's business, test the handoff in preview with a representative taking the chat and the booking, walk representatives through the chat inbox and the conversation score, then publish.
XP07.evidence: The Meeting Booking and Live Chat integrations give the concierge the ability to check availability, start a chat, and book a slot.

XP08.name: Custom routing rules on Marketo attributes
XP08.src: Experience League: Brand Concierge, Route conversations to representatives
XP08.scope: Build the routing rules in Marketo Qualifier that send a visitor to the right team by geography, product interest, company size or industry, set each rule's priority and representatives, and test them with sample visitors.
XP08.evidence: Custom routing evaluates the rules you build in Adobe Marketo Qualifier against the visitor's Marketo lead and company attributes.

XK14.name: Brand validation results in Frame.io review
XK14.src: Adobe for Business: Brand validation with Adobe Brand Intelligence
XK14.scope: Agree with your client's review leads at which step of their Frame.io reviews the brand validation results are read and what happens to an asset that fails before sign-off, then try the agreed steps on one real review.
XK14.evidence: Apply brand checks as assets move through review workflows, instead of running validation as a separate manual step.

XK15.name: Brand checks on production workflow outputs
XK15.src: Adobe for Business: Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise
XK15.scope: Agree with your client's production lead which production workflows have their outputs validated against brand guidelines, estimate the Operations the checks use at the planned volume, run a test batch through to the results in Frame.io, and agree which failed outputs are rerun before review.
XK15.evidence: Automatically validate production outputs against brand guidelines and display results in Frame.io for review and sign-off.

XK16.name: Instruct to Assemble rollout for designers in Figma
XK16.src: Adobe Firefly help: Instruct to Assemble
XK16.scope: Train your client's designers to run the Adobe Brand Intelligence plugin in Figma: choose the context, set the number of variants, review what it assembles, adjust single assets or regenerate with other assembly options, and agree how finished variants go on to review.
XK16.evidence: You can make manual adjustments to individual assets if needed, or regenerate variants with different assembly options.

XF01.name: AEM Assets Connector rollout for Figma designers
XF01.src: Experience League: Integrate AEM Assets with Figma
XF01.scope: Check that your client's AEM environment is on release 19149 or later, give the designers access to the agreed AEM Assets folders with the same company or federated Adobe ID they sign in with, roll out the AEM Assets Connector from the Figma Community, and test search, place, Check for updates and upload with the design team.
XF01.evidence: AEM Assets integrates natively with Figma, which allows designers to directly access the assets stored in AEM Assets from within the Figma user interface.

XF02.name: Save-back folders and export settings for Figma designs
XF02.src: Experience League: Integrate AEM Assets with Figma
XF02.scope: Agree with your client's DAM owner which AEM Assets folders take the designs uploaded from Figma, the file format, scale and quality each use needs, how the files are named and when designers run Check for updates, then write the short guide the design team follows.
XF02.evidence: The export configuration comprises the file format, scale, and quality.

XF03.name: Figma ad templates prepared for the GenStudio plugin
XF03.src: Experience League: Figma plugin for GenStudio for Performance Marketing
XF03.scope: Install the Firefly Enterprise and GenStudio plugin from the Figma community marketplace for your client's designers, set up their Figma ad files as sections and frames at the sizes Meta, LinkedIn and Display accept, map the field roles with at least one image, and generate, translate and export test variations to GenStudio for Performance Marketing.
XF03.evidence: Map Figma text elements to GenStudio for Performance Marketing fields, such as headline, body, on_image_text, and more.

XF04.name: Figma frames converted for GenStudio Photoshop
XF04.src: Experience League: Figma plugin for GenStudio for Performance Marketing
XF04.scope: Take the agreed Figma frames out of sections, convert them with the plugin to Photoshop documents for use with GenStudio Photoshop, open them in Photoshop, and rebuild with the designer what the conversion does not carry over, such as gradients, opacity percentages, strikethrough, superscript and subscript.
XF04.evidence: You can use the Figma plugin to convert a Figma frame, multiple frames, or an entire document to Photoshop format and export it for use with GenStudio Photoshop.
XF04.ext: GenStudio Photoshop from Adobe Exchange, in Photoshop 25.6.0 or later

XF05.name: Figma designs imported into Adobe Express
XF05.src: Adobe Help: Import Figma designs into Adobe Express
XF05.scope: Check that your client's Express users who import can use the Figma add-on (on enterprise plans through Admin Console roles), connect the Figma account of each person who imports, import the agreed frames with Native Import or Rasterize, fix the fonts the import summary marks Font Not Available and the shapes that came in as images, and hand the corrected designs over for templates.
XF05.evidence: Native Import: Imports supported content as editable Adobe Express elements.

XF06.name: Custom models for Figma designers
XF06.src: Adobe Firefly help: Use text to image to generate images in Figma
XF06.scope: Check that each of your client's Figma designers has the plugin, Firefly access and the custom models they have created, then with each designer pick their models in Text to image, generate images and place them on the Figma canvas, and walk them through the prompt guide for each model.
XF06.evidence: Select an Adobe or Partner model from the Model dropdown menu or choose a custom model you've created.

XR02.name: Commerce to ERP integration
XR02.src: Adobe Developer: Install Adobe Commerce integration starter kit
XR02.scope: Build the integration between Adobe Commerce and your client's ERP on Adobe's Commerce integration starter kit in App Builder: map order, customer, product and stock fields, deploy the actions for each, subscribe to the Commerce events, connect the actions to the ERP's APIs, set retries and test. Where a prebuilt connector on Adobe Exchange fits the ERP, install and configure it instead.
XR02.evidence: Integrating Adobe Commerce with your enterprise resource planning (ERP), order management system (OMS), or customer relationship management (CRM) is now easier with Adobe Commerce integration starter kit.
XR02.ext: an ERP with APIs the integration can call

XR03.name: Live ERP answers at checkout with webhooks
XR03.src: Adobe Developer: Adobe Commerce Webhooks overview
XR03.scope: Set up Commerce webhooks that call your client's ERP when Commerce needs an answer at once, such as order totals, taxes or payments, write the answer back into Commerce, set timeouts and what happens when the ERP does not answer, and test them under load.
XR03.evidence: Synchronous calls are required when Commerce needs to compute or validate something immediately (order totals, taxes, payments) using a 3rd-party endpoint and write the result back into Adobe Commerce.

XR04.name: Admin screens to run the back-office sync
XR04.src: Adobe Developer: Adobe Commerce Admin UI SDK overview
XR04.scope: Add pages to your client's Commerce Admin with the Admin UI SDK where the team sets up the back-office sync, sees what was sent and what failed, and sends a record again.
XR04.evidence: Integrate third-party systems - Connect to ERP, CRM, or warehouse management systems for data sync and operations management.

XR05.name: Product data from the PIM into Commerce
XR05.src: Adobe Developer: Enrich the shopping experience
XR05.scope: Map your client's PIM product attributes, categories and media to Commerce, build the starter kit's product actions in App Builder that write each create, update and delete to Commerce, run the first full load, and test that changes in the PIM reach the storefront.
XR05.evidence: This runtime action is responsible for notifying Adobe Commerce when an <object> is created, updated, or deleted in the external backoffice application.
XR05.ext: a PIM with APIs or events the integration can use

XR06.name: Commerce to order management integration
XR06.src: Adobe Developer: Install Adobe Commerce integration starter kit
XR06.scope: Build the integration between Adobe Commerce and your client's order management system on Adobe's Commerce integration starter kit in App Builder, or configure a prebuilt connector from Adobe Exchange where one fits: send each order, bring back order status and shipments with tracking numbers, set retries and test returns and cancellations.
XR06.evidence: Integrating Adobe Commerce with your enterprise resource planning (ERP), order management system (OMS), or customer relationship management (CRM) is now easier with Adobe Commerce integration starter kit.
XR06.ext: an order management system with APIs the integration can call

XR07.name: Live stock checks from the order management system
XR07.src: Adobe Developer: Adobe Commerce Webhooks overview
XR07.scope: Set up a Commerce webhook that asks your client's order management system for a product's stock status when a shopper adds it to the cart or checks out, write the answer back into Commerce, set what happens when the system does not answer, and test it under load.
XR07.evidence: As an example, the call requests a product's stock status to make sure it is available to be purchased.

XR08.name: Stock and shipment sync with the warehouse system
XR08.src: Adobe Developer: Starter kit data flows
XR08.scope: Map your client's warehouse locations to Commerce inventory sources, build the starter kit's stock and shipment actions in App Builder so stock quantities and shipments with tracking numbers reach Commerce, send orders to the warehouse system, and test a full order from purchase to shipment.
XR08.evidence: The starter kit supports the following data flows: Customers Orders Products Shipment Stock
XR08.ext: a warehouse management system with APIs the integration can call

ACO04.name: Commerce Optimizer Connector on Adobe Commerce
ACO04.src: Experience League: Get started with the Adobe Commerce Optimizer Connector
ACO04.scope: Uninstall Live Search, Product Recommendations and Catalog Service from your client's Commerce, install the Commerce Optimizer Connector with Composer, choose the websites, customer groups and store views to sync, turn on the integration, run the first sync and check the data in Optimizer.
ACO04.evidence: Install the Adobe Commerce Optimizer Connector package using Composer to connect your Adobe Commerce instance to Commerce Optimizer.

ACO05.name: B2B shared catalogs into Commerce Optimizer
ACO05.src: Experience League: Adobe Commerce Optimizer Connector overview
ACO05.scope: Install Adobe's Commerce Optimizer Connector for B2B on your client's Commerce, sync its shared catalogs, check each one shows as a private catalog view in Optimizer, and test what each company account sees.
ACO05.evidence: The separate Adobe Commerce Optimizer Connector for B2B extends the base connector to synchronize shared catalog configuration and automatically project custom shared catalogs as private catalog views.

ACO06.name: Product data from the PIM into Commerce Optimizer
ACO06.src: Adobe Developer: Data Ingestion API (Commerce Optimizer)
ACO06.scope: Define the product attribute metadata Optimizer needs for your client's catalog, map the PIM's products, categories and prices to the Data Ingestion API, build the job that sends creates, updates and deletes, run the first full load and check the Data Sync page.
ACO06.evidence: The Data Ingestion API is designed to be used by backend applications to manage product data.
ACO06.ext: a PIM with APIs or exports the job can read

ACO07.name: Catalog sync from the other commerce platform
ACO07.src: Experience League: Adobe Commerce Optimizer integrations
ACO07.scope: Set up Adobe's Commerce Salesforce Connector in App Builder for your client's Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C, or a sync job on the Data Ingestion API for another platform, schedule the syncs, run the first full load and check catalog and prices in Optimizer.
ACO07.evidence: The Commerce Salesforce Connector (built on Adobe App Builder) syncs catalog and price data from Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C into Adobe Commerce Optimizer so you can use Adobe storefront and merchandising capabilities without replatforming your Salesforce commerce backend.

ACO08.name: Cart and checkout hand-off to the other commerce platform
ACO08.src: Experience League: Adobe Commerce Optimizer integrations
ACO08.scope: Build the custom integration that hands your client's shoppers from the Optimizer storefront to the other platform's accounts, cart and checkout with API Mesh, App Builder or its APIs, adapting Adobe's checkout starter kit for Salesforce Commerce Cloud where it applies, and test a full order.
ACO08.evidence: Integration with the host platform is a custom implementation, using API Mesh, App Builder, direct APIs, or a combination of these tools.

ACO09.name: Storefront on Edge Delivery for Commerce Optimizer
ACO09.src: Experience League: Set up your storefront (Commerce Optimizer)
ACO09.scope: Create your client's storefront project on Edge Delivery Services with Adobe's Site Creator, point it at the Optimizer instance, catalog view and locale, build the product detail, search and category pages from Adobe's ready-made storefront parts, brand them and test them against the agreed pages.
ACO09.evidence: This guide walks you through setting up a storefront for your Adobe Commerce Optimizer instance using Adobe Edge Delivery Services.

ACO11.name: Optimizer storefront SEO and launch checklist
ACO11.src: Experience League: Adobe Commerce Storefront launch checklist
ACO11.scope: Run the launch checklist for your client's Optimizer storefront on Edge Delivery Services. Verify metadata, redirects and indexing in staging, test product discovery and the cart and checkout hand-off to the commerce backend, and document the DNS, CDN and publishing sequence and rollback plan.
ACO11.evidence: Complete these steps before production traffic reaches your Adobe Commerce Storefront (EDS).

ACO12.name: Optimizer storefront events to Experience Platform
ACO12.src: Experience League: Adobe Experience Platform for Commerce Storefront
ACO12.scope: Configure your client's Adobe organization and datastream on the Optimizer storefront and connect the client's consent platform. Test product views and cart actions and validate purchase events where the checkout integration emits them. Verify the agreed events reach the Experience Platform dataset.
ACO12.evidence: This integration allows your storefront to send commerce events (product views, purchases, cart actions) directly to the Experience Platform Edge Network

ACO10.name: Product images from AEM Assets with Product Visuals
ACO10.src: Experience League: Adobe Commerce Optimizer integrations
ACO10.scope: Configure AEM Assets for Commerce Optimizer to turn on Product Visuals, agree with your client's DAM owner how product images carry their SKU and are approved, and check that approved images show on the storefront.
ACO10.evidence: The integration matches assets to products by SKU.

MBI01.name: Commerce database connection for Commerce Intelligence
MBI01.src: Experience League: Connect your Adobe Commerce database
MBI01.scope: Connect your client's Commerce database to Commerce Intelligence through an SSH tunnel, with a read-only database user and the host key checked, choose the first tables to sync and check the first sync.
MBI01.evidence: As the Adobe Commerce database is based on MySQL, you can connect it to Commerce Intelligence through a direct connection , cPanel , or via an SSH tunnel .

MBI06.name: Salesforce data into Commerce Intelligence
MBI06.src: Experience League: Salesforce in Commerce Intelligence
MBI06.scope: Connect your client's Salesforce to Commerce Intelligence with a Salesforce user that can read the agreed objects, choose the tables to sync and join them to the Commerce data for the agreed reports.
MBI06.evidence: Connecting your Salesforce data enables a range of analyses, from scoring and optimizing leads to hitting your goals for converted opportunities.

MBI07.name: Google Ads cost data into Commerce Intelligence
MBI07.src: Experience League: Google Adwords in Commerce Intelligence
MBI07.scope: Connect your client's Google Ads account to Commerce Intelligence, check that campaign tracking on the storefront ties orders to campaigns, and build the report of campaign cost against the lifetime value of the customers each campaign brought.
MBI07.evidence: you can measure campaign ROI by marrying your advertising cost and the customer lifetime value (CLV) of users acquired from your campaigns.
